briefing.hook: At 4:50 AM the research station on Harrow Inlet reported that its lead marine scientist, Dr. Vera Lindqvist, had vanished from a locked cabin. A torn note, an overturned chair, and her phone left on the table suggested a struggle.
briefing.context: Vera had been leading a controversial study funded by a private partner, Adrian Voss, whose data practices she had recently begun to question. The station is small, remote, and reachable only by boat.
briefing.tension: A missing person in a locked room reads like abduction. But the only person who could have taken her is also the one who appears to have staged the scene — and no one is certain which.
briefing.objective: Determine whether Vera was taken, whether she left on her own, and if so, why she would make herself disappear.

truth.incident: Vera staged her own disappearance. She had discovered that Adrian Voss was falsifying the research data to secure a lucrative renewal, and that she was being positioned to co-sign the fraudulent results. Rather than blow the whistle and be blamed, she arranged her own vanishing: withdrew funds under a second identity she had quietly built, staged a struggle in the cabin, took her own boat out, scuttled it, and slipped away by a service route she had pre-arranged.
truth.whatHappened: Vera left under her own power after staging the scene. She used a decoy phone, a second identity, and a pre-planned exit route. She intended to surface once the fraudulent study could no longer be pinned on her.
truth.motive: To escape being coerced into co-signing falsified research and to expose Adrian without becoming the scapegoat.
truth.method: Second identity, advance cash withdrawal, staged struggle, self-scuttled boat, pre-arranged land route.
truth.centralTwist: The apparent victim of an abduction is the author of her own disappearance.
truth.finalTruth: There was no abduction. Vera left deliberately, and the 'struggle' was a prop.

evidence.name: Boathouse Log
evidence.description: The log shows Vera's boat leaving under its own power at 02:10 and found scuttled, empty, at 04:40.

evidence.name: Withdrawal Record
evidence.description: A large cash withdrawal three days before the vanishing, under a name no staff member recognizes.

evidence.name: Scene Photographs
evidence.description: The 'struggle' shows an overturned chair and torn note arranged deliberately; no forensic sign of a fight.

evidence.name: Research Audit
evidence.description: An internal audit shows entries in Adrian's dataset that do not match the raw samples Vera collected.

evidence.name: Decoy Phone
evidence.description: The phone left on the table was an old, deactivated model — not Vera's active device.

questions.text: The night she vanished — what do you remember?

mateo.text: I was asleep. I heard and saw nothing.
She said she was going for a walk to think. That was the last I saw her.
She'd been talking about starting over for weeks. I think she planned this.

sofia.text: I didn't see a thing out of place.
The chair was overturned, the note torn — but something about it felt arranged.
There was no sign of a real fight. The scene looked put together.

inspector.text: The boat left under power and came back scuttled the same night. That is not how abductions usually go.
The physical record does not yet point to anyone else taking her.

questions.text: What did the boathouse log show?

inspector.text: Her boat left under its own power at 02:10 and was found scuttled, empty, hours later.
The log is unusual. I want to compare it against the tide tables.

questions.text: Your study with Vera — any problems with the data?

adrian.text: The data is pristine. Vera agreed with every result.
There were minor discrepancies. Nothing that changes the conclusions.
You should ask the statisticians, not me.

questions.text: The scene looked like a struggle — what did you actually see?

sofia.text: It was a real fight, I'm sure of it.
The chair was knocked over, but the room was too tidy for a struggle.
The note was torn neatly. This was arranged to look like a struggle.

mateo.text: She mentioned having savings put aside. I didn't ask where.
I wouldn't know about her money.
She had cash that didn't match her salary. She was ready to leave.

questions.text: The phone left behind — was it actually hers?

inspector.text: No. It was an old, deactivated model — a decoy left on purpose.
The device doesn't match her current account. Odd.

questions.text: Did Vera ever talk about wanting to disappear and start over?

mateo.text: She joked about it. I thought it was stress.
She was serious. She wanted out of the study and out of Adrian's reach.
I don't want to speculate about a missing person.

sofia.text: She told me once she'd 'made plans that nobody could undo.'
She seemed to have something settled, like she'd already decided.

questions.text: Vera accused you of falsifying the data. Was she right?

adrian.text: Absolutely not. She was mistaken, or jealous.
There were adjustments. Any study has them.
Some entries were smoothed. She found out, and she was going to ruin the renewal.

contradictions.description: The 'struggle' in the cabin looks arranged rather than the result of a real fight.
A large withdrawal was made under a name no one at the station recognizes.
The boat left under power and returned scuttled the same night — consistent with someone leaving and sinking it themselves.
Vera flagged falsified data attributed to Adrian weeks before she vanished.
The phone 'left behind' was a deactivated decoy, not Vera's active device.

options.label: Vera staged her own disappearance and left.
She fled after a personal dispute.
To escape being coerced into falsified research.
Out of fear of her partner.

reveal.headline: No one took Vera. She took herself.
narrative: Vera Lindqvist staged her own disappearance.
She had quietly built a second identity and withdrawn cash in advance, then arranged a struggle in the cabin with an overturned chair, a torn note, and a deactivated decoy phone.
She left on her own boat, scuttled it herself near the inlet mouth, and slipped away by a route she had pre-planned.
The motive was escape: she had discovered Adrian falsifying the research data and was being positioned to co-sign the fraudulent results.
Mateo had guessed but said nothing from loyalty. Adrian's panic was about exposure, not her safety. Sofia simply reported a scene that looked like a crime because it was built to.

truthBreakdown.fact: The struggle was arranged, not real.
She held a second identity and withdrew cash early.

The abandoned phone was a decoy.
